title: GPS: GNN-Based Two-Stage Pre-Scheduling Loop Mapping Method on CGRAs
problem: Coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) compilers must generate effective loop mappings for complex applications within tight time budgets, but the large search space makes optimal mapping intractable.
motivation: CGRAs are promising for AI acceleration, but compiler speed is a critical bottleneck preventing adoption; existing techniques either produce poor mappings quickly or good mappings slowly.
method: GPS finds efficient loop mappings for CGRAs in two stages. First, it uses Integer Linear Programming—a mathematical method that systematically searches for optimal solutions within constraints—to identify promising regions and set initial boundaries. Second, it applies a Graph Neural Network, a machine learning approach that learns patterns from graph-structured data, to explore within those boundaries and prune away poor mappings while refining the best ones. This two-stage combination significantly reduces the search space, enabling the compiler to find good mappings faster while maintaining or improving their quality.
key_novelty: GPS combines a first stage of Integer Linear Programming with a second stage of Graph Neural Network refinement to reduce the CGRA loop mapping search space, achieving faster compilation while maintaining or improving solution quality.
contributions: GNN-based pre-scheduling method to reduce ILP search space
Two-stage mapping approach combining learning and optimization
1106.8x compilation time reduction vs. existing techniques
primary_theme: GNN-assisted ILP for fast CGRA loop mapping
